title: The dashboard, from route to live readout
summary: The `/` route is a five-line server shim; everything the operator sees on the home screen — the greeting, the run controls, the readiness rollup and the board summary — is assembled by one client component, `GarrisonHome`, from state the app shell already holds plus a single board fetch.

states.label: Dashboard
states.description: The drillbook asks that this page present operative status, readiness, the board summary, quick actions and run controls without overlap, clipping or misleading status. It is the app's home route (`/`), and the whole of it renders from one component.

steps.title: The route is a shim onto one client component
steps.description: Navigating to `/` lands on a server component that does nothing but mount `GarrisonHome`. There is no data-loading in the route itself: the dashboard is a client component that reads everything it needs from the shell context, which is why the route file is five lines long.

steps.title: Everything on the page comes from the shell context
steps.description: `GarrisonHome` pulls the active composition, the runner's live state, the vault seal and the `runAction` dispatcher out of `useAppShell()`. Nothing here fetches the composition — the shell has already loaded it — so the dashboard is a pure render over shared state, and a null composition is the loading branch just below.

steps.title: Run controls sit in the command deck
steps.description: The primary control is one button that dispatches `runAction("up")` — install Fittings, verify, then start — relabelling itself "Restart operative" while a run is live. The Stop button appears only when the status is `running`, so the operator never sees a stop control for something that is not up. Both disable while `busy`.

steps.title: Readiness rolls four checks into one panel
steps.description: The readiness panel is the operator's go/no-go glance: faculties stationed, capability wiring, vault seal, verify hooks. Capability wiring is the one that turns alarm-toned — an unresolved `consumes`/`provides` edge is the failure that keeps an operative from assembling — so it reads its count straight off `composition.capabilityIssues`.

steps.title: The board summary is the page's only live fetch
steps.description: The Board panel is the one part of the dashboard that reaches out over the network: it polls `/api/board/summary` on mount and every 30 seconds, and swallows a failed fetch on purpose — a home-screen panel for a board that simply is not running should stay quiet, not raise an error banner. Loading and failure both fall through to the idle state.
